claim: For every compact metric space \(K\), finite positive Radon measure \(\mu\) on \(K\), and \(1\le p<\infty\), write \(\mu=\mu_{\mathrm{at}}+\mu_{\mathrm{c}}\) for its atomic and nonatomic parts and let \(J_\mu:C(K)\to L^p(\mu)\) be the canonical inclusion. Then its essential norm, the operator-norm distance to compact operators, is exactly \(\|J_\mu\|_{\mathrm{ess}}=\mu_{\mathrm{c}}(K)^{1/p}\).
integrity: The proof is analytic and self-contained modulo standard measure-isomorphism and \(L^p\)-density facts. No numerical computation is used. The two closest embedding sources were assessed from accessible abstracts only; no claim of exhaustive full-text exclusion is made.
scientific_limitations: Compact metric \(K\), finite positive Radon measure \(\mu\), and \(1\le p<\infty\) only. The formula does not cover \(p=\infty\) or arbitrary nonstandard measure spaces. A residual priority risk remains for an unindexed exact essential-norm theorem.
title: Essential norm of the canonical \(C(K)\)-to-\(L^p(\mu)\) embedding is the diffuse mass
